PURPOSE: Add the subordinate clause - it has a verb but still cannot stand alone.
PREP: Whiteboards out; both earlier rules are restated in the I do.

i_do.title: The clause that cannot stand alone
i_do.rule: A main clause has a verb and stands alone. A subordinate clause has a verb but cannot.
i_do.example: Because the river rose - rose is the verb, but it cannot stand alone, so it is a subordinate clause.
items: Subordinate openers: because, when, although, if, while.
A verb is the doing or being word. A phrase has none at all.
i_do.footer: You will label three of them
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: Because the river rose is a subordinate clause; the verb is rose.
1. SAY: "A clause has its own verb. A main clause stands alone, and a subordinate clause has a verb but still cannot."
2. MODEL: point at rose. SAY: "Rose is the doing word, so this group is a clause, not a phrase."
3. MODEL: read it aloud alone. SAY: "Because the river rose - that leaves me waiting, so it is subordinate, not main."
4. ASK: "Which word makes it need more?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: because.
TRAP: calling it a phrase because it feels unfinished. Fix: find rose, name it as the verb, then label it a clause.

Purpose: separate the two kinds of clause; earlier rules restated for absentees. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]
